text: I'm doing thematic analysis on 14 semi-structured interviews with food delivery couriers, mostly about how they make sense of the dispatch algorithm (folk theories, workarounds, pay uncertainty). Transcripts come out of otter as speaker turns, Interviewer / P01 etc. I have a first-pass codebook of 7 codes, each with a name and a one or two sentence definition. I want a page where I read one participant at a time, select a passage and tag it with a code, and the coded passages stay tinted in that code's colour. Codebook on the side with the definitions visible so i'm not flipping back to the google doc. Use fake data for now, 3 participants is fine, I'll paste mine in later.

bug: when I click another code the highlight on the previous passage disappears. every coded passage needs to stay tinted. also one passage can have two codes (folk theory + distrust overlap constantly), just show the overlap somehow. and I need a way to take a code off a passage, i misclick a lot

can you put counts next to each code in the sidebar, number of segments and how many participants it shows up in. I want to see at a glance if something like workaround is one chatty person or everyone
I keep making new codes as I go (its partly inductive), let me add a code with a name and definition from the sidebar without editing the file

add a filter: click a code and see only the turns coded with it, across all participants not just the one I'm on, with the participant id on each turn. and from there let me jump back to that spot in the full transcript

last thing, export the coded segments as csv - participant, turn number, speaker, code, quoted text. my advisor wants it in a spreadsheet. and please save to localstorage, I lost an afternoon of coding when chrome restarted lol
